body.statement:
For every \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\), translate \(Q[S_0](s_0;x_0)\) to \(Q=P((S_0)_{x_0}=s_0)\). For every ordinary identifying collection \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\), the embedded protocols \(S_{B_i}\) are legal SELECT--RAND--READ protocols, every assignment slice satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S_{B_i},\ell_{i,b})
 =Q[V\setminus B_i](\mathord\cdot;b)=P_b(V\setminus B_i),
\]
and the generic acquired collection containing these protocols and all labels in \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}\) has distinct-protocol cost \(\sum_{B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\); its acquired laws therefore contain the complete ordinary identifying family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\). Conversely, from every accepted uniform certificate \(E\) in \(\iota(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}})\), augment protocols by the missing zero-cost READ actions and coalesce equal RAND-endpoint sets to obtain \(\mathbf B(E)\). The full assignment slices generate \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E)}\), this family identifies \(Q[S_0](\mathord\cdot;x_0)\), and
\[
 \sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E)}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v
 \le \operatorname{Cost}(E),
\]
with equality when \(E\) has at most one protocol mask for each RAND-endpoint set. Consequently the minimum ordinary design cost is no greater than \(\operatorname{Opt}\) whenever the embedded uniform-certificate problem is feasible. No converse feasibility implication or equality of optimum costs is asserted.
body.justification: The two-way embedding matches the ordinary \(Q[S]\) target and source-family semantics before certifying legality, acceptance, and exact cost preservation.
body.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5, Lemma 3 on page 8, Lemma 7 on page 12, and Proposition 3 on page 16 concern ordinary intervention collections and their fixed \(Q[S]\) source families. They do not prove the two-way Layer-2.5 translation with explicit oracle-returned support, finite assignment labels, adequate READ records, complete-run acceptance, and exact protocol-cost preservation established here.
body.consumer: The equivalence transfers the ordinary hardness frontier without silently enlarging the source family or changing the causal query.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\).  The translation definition identifies the ordinary target with the single-world Layer-2.5 event
\[
 Q=P((S_0)_{x_0}=s_0).
\]
For a distinct intervention set \(B\), the embedded protocol is
\[
 S_B=\{s\}\cup\{r_v:v\in B\}\cup\{\rho_v:v\in V\}.
\]
It contains exactly one fresh-unit SELECT.  Every mechanism is used at most once, SELECT precedes every other action, the remaining actions follow causal order, and the embedded catalogue has no conflicts.  By the physical-compatibility clause in the embedding, \(S_B\) satisfies CTF-REALIZE.  Hence \(S_B\in\Pi\).

The RAND actions are mutually independent and uniform on their finite allowed domains.  Thus, for every \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\),
\[
 P_{S_B}(L_B=b)=\prod_{v\in B}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}>0.
\]
All vertices are READ, so measured ancestry holds.  The intervention and consistency semantics recorded in the embedding and label-slice definitions then give, without division by a zero-probability event,
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S_B,\ell_{B,b})
 =P_b(V\setminus B)
 =Q[V\setminus B](\mathord\cdot;b).
\]
Taking all \(b\) and all distinct \(B\) therefore supplies exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\), which identifies the ordinary target by the definition of an ordinary identifying collection.  SELECT and all READ actions have zero cost, whereas \(c(r_v)=\kappa_v\).  Since slices share the cost of their protocol and duplicate intervention sets are coalesced,
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{0,\mathbf B})
 =\sum_{B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}
   \sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v.
\]

Conversely, let \(E\) be accepted in the embedded catalogue.  A decoded protocol has one SELECT, no CTF-RAND action, some RAND-endpoint set \(B\), and some READ mask.  Add every missing zero-cost READ action after its prerequisites.  The resulting protocol is exactly \(S_B\), is legal by the preceding argument, and has the same action cost.  If two original protocol masks differ only in their READ masks, their augmentations coincide; coalescing them can only decrease cost because all action costs are nonnegative.  Hence
\[
 \sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E)}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v
 \le \operatorname{Cost}(E),
\]
and equality holds when no two masks have the same RAND-endpoint set.

For each retained \(B\), uniform RAND support makes every \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\) a positive slice, and the slice identity above shows that these slices are exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E)}\).  The full-READ law also reproduces every source used by the accepted certificate by projection and by the same positive conditioning event.  Therefore the accepted factor derivations remain valid after augmentation.  In this single-world translation, erasing the redundant counterfactual world labels from each ancestor and district restriction leaves the ordinary identification recursion on the kernels \(Q[V\setminus B](\mathord\cdot;b)\).  Induction over the finite accepted restriction sequence shows that this ordinary recursion succeeds, so \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E)}\) identifies \(Q[S_0](\mathord\cdot;x_0)\).

Apply the cost inequality to every accepted uniform certificate and then take the infimum.  The minimum ordinary identifying-collection cost is at most \(\operatorname{Opt}\).  The forward construction above supplies a generic physical acquisition with the ordinary cost, but the two-source value-matching example in the branchwise-normalization proof shows why it need not yield one source slice uniform over every equality-type branch.  Thus the reverse inequality, uniform feasibility, and equality of optima do not follow.
